articles.title: UK Visa Changes: What You Need to Know in 2025
articles.excerpt: Recent Home Office reforms affect Skilled Worker visas, family routes, and student extensions. We break down what has changed and what it means for you.
body: The UK immigration system continues to evolve, and 2025 has brought a number of important updates that affect individuals, families, and employers alike. Understanding how these changes apply to your circumstances is the first step to planning with confidence.

For those on the Skilled Worker route, salary thresholds, sponsorship requirements, and eligibility criteria are areas where even small changes can have a significant impact. Employers holding a sponsor licence should review their obligations carefully to remain compliant.

Family and partner routes remain one of the most common ways to settle in the UK, but applications are document-heavy and unforgiving of small errors. Preparing a complete, well-evidenced application from the outset saves both time and stress.

Students and recent graduates should be aware of how extensions and post-study work options interact with longer-term settlement plans. The right decision now can make future applications far more straightforward.
Every case turns on its own facts. If you would like tailored advice on how these changes affect you, our bilingual team is here to help — in English or Korean.

articles.title: Self-Assessment Deadline Guide for UK Residents
articles.excerpt: A clear guide to HMRC self-assessment deadlines, penalties, and how to file correctly — whether you are employed, self-employed, or a landlord.
body: Filing a Self-Assessment tax return is an annual obligation for many UK residents, yet the rules around who needs to file, when, and how are a frequent source of confusion.

Missing a deadline can lead to automatic penalties that grow over time, even when no tax is ultimately owed. Knowing the key dates for registration, online filing, and payment is essential to staying on the right side of HMRC.

Your filing position depends on your circumstances. Employees, the self-employed, company directors, and landlords each face different considerations, and income from more than one source often needs careful handling.
Good record-keeping throughout the year makes the process far simpler and helps ensure you claim every allowance and expense you are entitled to.
If you are unsure whether you need to file, or would like us to prepare and submit your return for you, our accounting team can guide you through every step.

articles.title: Setting Up a Business in the UK: A Step-by-Step Guide
articles.excerpt: From choosing the right company structure to registering at Companies House — everything you need to start your UK business with confidence.
body: Starting a business in the UK is an exciting step, and getting the foundations right from day one makes everything that follows easier.

One of the first decisions is choosing the right structure — sole trader, partnership, or limited company. Each has different implications for liability, tax, and administration, and the best choice depends on your plans and appetite for risk.

Registering a limited company at Companies House is straightforward in principle, but decisions about share structure, directors, and governance are easier to get right at the start than to unwind later.
Beyond registration, new businesses need to consider tax registration, bookkeeping, and any regulatory requirements specific to their sector.
Our combined legal and accounting team can help you establish your business on solid footing — and support you as it grows. Get in touch to discuss your plans.
